record.original_question: Construct explicit presentations of a virtual biquandle that uses the given linear non-commutative representation at classical crossings together with a genuinely informative algebraic structure at virtual crossings.

evidence.quote: Construct presentations of the virtual biquandle with the a linear (non-commutative) representation at classical crossings and some interesting structure at virtual crossings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A virtual biquandle is a set $X$ equipped with four binary operations $\triangleright, \triangleright^{-1}, \blacktriangleright, \blacktriangleright^{-1}: X \times X \to X$ (encoding the labelings at classical crossings) together with an invertible unary operation $f: X \to X$ (encoding the labeling at virtual crossings), such that the operations satisfy the algebraic axioms corresponding to invariance under all generalized Reidemeister moves for virtual link diagrams (the classical Reidemeister moves I, II, III; the virtual Reidemeister moves V1, V2, V3; and the mixed move involving one classical and two virtual crossings).

A linear (non-commutative) representation at classical crossings is a virtual biquandle structure on a module $X$ over an associative (possibly non-commutative) ring $R$ such that the operations $\triangleright$ and $\blacktriangleright$ are given by $R$-linear formulas of the form
$$ a \triangleright b = a\,S + b\,T, \qquad a \blacktriangleright b = a\,U + b\,V $$
for fixed elements $S, T, U, V \in R$ (or, more generally, by linear endomorphisms of $X \oplus X$), so that the resulting set-theoretic Yang–Baxter operator at classical crossings is linear and non-commutative.

Construct an explicit presentation of a virtual biquandle in which:
1. the operations at classical crossings form such a linear non-commutative representation, and
2. the unary operation $f$ at virtual crossings is given by a genuinely non-trivial algebraic structure (i.e., not merely the identity or a scalar map, but a structurally informative operation that interacts non-trivially with the classical operations through the mixed Reidemeister move).

Exhibit the underlying ring $R$, the module $X$, the constants $S, T, U, V$, and the map $f$, and verify that all virtual biquandle axioms are satisfied.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a well-known list of unsolved problems in virtual knot theory. Recent work (2023–2025) on virtual biquandles, group biquandles, and biquandle cocycle quiver representations develops related algebraic structures, but no source explicitly identifies a fully satisfactory construction of a virtual biquandle combining a linear non-commutative representation at classical crossings with a genuinely informative structure at virtual crossings. Status appears unresolved in published literature.
